title: GRO-Seq/BRIC-Seq/Bru-Seq/BruChase-Seq
scope: Illumina explanatory schematic: a single GRO-Seq-like nuclear run-on → RNA fragmentation → antibody-bead enrichment → terminal processing → amplified cDNA route. The grouped BRIC-Seq caption is retained as an observation but its implementation is resolved separately using Tani et al. (full text). Bru-Seq and BruChase-Seq are distinct named methods, supported here only at the labeling/sequencing and pulse-chase/sequencing level of the supplied Paulsen et al. abstract. Additional variant routes below are paper-reported qualifications, not branches drawn in the PNG or a universal family protocol.

states.label: Nuclear transcription complexes bearing nascent RNA (GRO-Seq)

For the scoped Core implementation, these are transcriptionally engaged polymerases in isolated nuclei; the cartoon does not itself draw a nuclear boundary.

operations.label: Run-on with analog
operations.description: In the GRO-Seq implementation, transcriptionally engaged polymerases in isolated nuclei extend their associated nascent RNAs using Br-UTP, producing BrU-tagged RNA. Core reports this nuclear run-on under conditions prohibiting new initiation; the figure simply labels it Run-on with analog.
operations.mechanism: Polymerase-mediated RNA extension with the ribonucleotide analog BrUTP.
operations.information_effect: BrU incorporation associates RNA with transcription complexes capable of extension during the run-on. The RNAPII focus comes from the card; the analog itself is not an RNAPII-specific tag.

operations.label: Bead coated with α-BrdUTP antibody
operations.description: The hydrolyzed RNA mixture contacts antibody-coated beads and yields bead-retained BrU-containing RNA. The figure labels the support α-BrdUTP antibody; the primary GRO-Seq paper identifies the selected material as BrU-containing nuclear-run-on RNA.
operations.mechanism: Antibody affinity selection for the BrU analog incorporated into RNA. This does not imply that free BrUTP or a bromodeoxyuridine-containing DNA product is the analyte.
operations.information_effect: Enrichment links retained RNA sequence to analog incorporation in the preceding run-on. Recognition is chemical, rather than a direct test of polymerase identity or perfect biological specificity. The single bead icon abstracts immunopurification; it is not a claim about the number of selection rounds, and no discarded-fraction branch is drawn.

operations.label: BrU labeling, chase and time-point RNA isolation (BRIC-Seq; paper-reported)
operations.description: BrU is added to culture medium to label endogenous RNA. After removal of BrU-containing medium, cells are harvested at successive chase times and total RNA is isolated. This produces time-indexed extracts containing the surviving labeled cohort. No nuclear run-on is inserted into this route.
operations.mechanism: Endogenous transcription incorporates label during cell-culture BrU exposure, followed by a chase after label removal.
operations.information_effect: The BrU mark defines a pre-existing cohort whose remaining abundance changes during the chase. Collection time remains part of each sample’s association.

evidence.quote: We used nuclear run-on assays (NRO) to extend nascent RNAs that are associated with transcriptionally engaged polymerases under conditions where new initiation is prohibited. To specifically isolate NRO-RNA, we added a ribonucleotide analog [5-bromouridine 5′-triphosphate (BrUTP)] to BrU-tag nascent RNA during the run-on step (fig. S1).

The length of the polynucleotide was kept short, and the NRO-RNA was chemically hydrolyzed into short fragments (∼100 bases) to facilitate high-resolution mapping of the polymerase origin at the time of assay (8).
BrU-containing NRO-RNA was triple-selected through immunopurification with an antibody that is specific for this nucleotide analog

A NRO-cDNA library was then prepared for sequencing from what represents the 5′ end of the fragmented, BrU-incorporated RNA molecule by using the Illumina high-throughput sequencing platform. The origin and the orientation of the RNAs and therefore the associated transcriptionally engaged polymerases were documented genome-wide by mapping the reads to the reference human genome (8).
After cap removal and end repair, the eluted RNA is reverse-transcribed to cDNA.

method_scopes.rationale: Distinct method, not an alias for GRO-Seq. Although BRIC appears in the drawing’s lower-left caption, Tani describes endogenous cell-culture BrU labeling, label removal and sequential RNA harvests, BrU-RNA immunopurification, then sequencing-library construction and decay measurements. These paper-supported operations qualify the grouped picture. The GRO nuclear run-on, pre-capture hydrolysis and cap-removal/end-repair block are not assigned to BRIC from this schematic.

corrections.primary_statement: Tani’s BRIC-Seq labels endogenous RNA by adding BrU to cell-culture medium, removes the label and isolates total RNA at sequential times, then immunopurifies BrU-RNA and constructs RNA-seq libraries. The BRIC scope and added variant route explicitly follow that primary implementation; the depicted GRO operations are retained for GRO rather than silently made universal.

corrections.diagram_observation: The capture support is labeled Bead coated with α-BrdUTP antibody, and the incoming RNA pieces contain red-star analog marks. The label does not specify a clone or the chemistry of a bound triphosphate.
corrections.primary_statement: Core reports immunopurification of BrU-containing nuclear-run-on RNA using an antibody specific for the analog. Accordingly o_capture is interpreted as affinity enrichment of incorporated BrU in RNA; the drawing’s α-BrdUTP wording is preserved as a label. Tani separately identifies an anti-BrdU antibody that also recognizes BrU for BRIC, without establishing that the exact same antibody implementation is used by GRO.
